recommendation: Keep the audit as-is and do not reintroduce MedicinalProductDefinition.administrableProduct unless BR&R explicitly reverses the later FHIR-31859 direct-route/no-bidirectional-link design.
issue_request: FHIR-28915 was Published/Persuasive and requested a simpler MedicinalProductDefinition representation for applications that only need licensed route, with a route code or full AdministrableProductDefinition reference but not both.
initial_application: Commit 322e216d548de8d681323e54e3082f15f7d8f07b initially applied FHIR-28915 by adding MedicinalProductDefinition.administrableProduct to the then-authoritative spreadsheet and examples.
additional_context: FHIR-31859 was a later Published/Persuasive BR&R decision to remove bidirectional product links. Its implementation replaced the MPD administrableProduct backbone/reference with direct MedicinalProductDefinition.route, and current APD source carries the APD-to-MPD formOf reference plus apd-1 to prevent duplicate route use. FHIR-28581 is broader background showing BR&R kept separate medication-definition resources while exposing common attributes such as route directly for simple cases.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because current source/fhir.ini keeps MPD and APD in build scope, MPD has a repeatable route element for the simple licensed route, and APD has the constraint text/expression that prevents using APD route when the linked MPD already carries route.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive BR&R issue removing bidirectional product links; it explains why the originally requested MPD-to-APD reference/backbone is no longer present.
Broader medication-definition consolidation debate; it records the rationale for exposing common attributes, including routes, directly while preserving separate detailed resources.
